newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index volatilities move back up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index volatilities move back up.

text.p: Volatilities in major U.S. stock index options moved sharply higher Monday, traders said.
Volatilities had moved lower last week, particularly Thursday, ahead of a three-day holiday weekend in the United States. The market closed early Thursday.
"There's not much going on except they're pumping up volatility again," a trader in S&P 100 index options said.
By about 1145 CDT/1645 GMT, the volatility index .VIX, one measure of volatility in OEX options, was up 1.23 points, or about six percent, at 21.50.
The VIX had risen intraday to 21.90.
Despite the pickup in volatility, the VIX remained well below its recent peaks above 24.
Traders said order flows were fairly steady in both puts and calls as the market rallied and then cut its gains.
The Dow industrial average was ahead 12 points at 7,908 after reaching 7,951 intraday.
Among broader indexes, the OEX gained 2.38 to 896. It had reached 901.66.
The S&P 500 .SPX added 1.29 to 918.21, after reaching 923.26.
The intraday peaks for all three indexes were records.
Jerry Hegarty, an options analyst at Thomson Financial Services, said he expected late-session strength to take the market up near its session peaks by the close.
He said the OEX was "vastly" outperforming S&P 500 futures, which was bullish for OEX July calls. September S&P 500 futures were down 1.35 at 926.40.
The most active OEX July call was the July 900, which traded about 5,600 contracts. The July 920 call traded 3,465 and the July 910 call traded 3,115.

Among SPX options, the July 870 put traded a heavy 12,600 contracts. Other busy puts included the August 880 with volume of 9,500 contracts, the July 925 with volume of 7,945 and the July 900 with volume of 3,155.
The SPX July 925 call traded 8,875 contracts and the July 950 call traded about 5,750.
